name: comp-510
title: Pricing Calendar
description: A tall calendar showing November and December stacked, with a small dollar price beneath every available day. Nights under a hundred dollars are tinted green, days without a price are dimmed and unclickable, and a chosen day fills white.
use: Travellers compare nightly costs before choosing dates, so price needs to sit on the calendar.
avoid: Prices are random mock figures created on load, so they are not real and differ on every visit.
a11y: Day buttons carry the date and price as text, but cheap nights are marked by green colour alone with no words. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two month blocks share a bordered black panel, each with a centred name, weekday initials and large square day cells. Each available day carries the number above a tiny dollar figure, some in emerald green, and the selected day sits in a solid white circle.
behaves: Clicking an available day circles it white while hovering fades a light square behind a day. The arrows turn both months together, and days with no price data cannot be pressed at all.
customise: The price generator, the 180-day window and the $100 green threshold live in the file; real prices or another highlight rule means editing the source.
weight: light: Two month grids and 180 generated prices; nothing animates.
demo: November and December 2026 with random nightly prices between $80 and $200; 14 November selected.
issues: Prices are random mock values regenerated on every page load.
Cheap nights are signalled by colour alone, so colour-blind users miss the cue.
The calendar is small in a wide empty stage, making prices hard to read.
The caption credits the calendar library instead of describing the prices.
polishWhy: Prices on dates read well in concept, but tiny type and random mock figures hold it back.

frames.note: Calendar is small and centred in a large empty stage, so the price text is barely legible.
